related_resources.reason: Emily Riehl, Category Theory in Context (2016)
Brendan Fong and David I. Spivak, Seven Sketches in Compositionality (2018)
Samuel Eilenberg and Saunders Mac Lane, General Theory of Natural Equivalences (1945)

description: Defines covariant and contravariant functors through the functor laws, forgetful and powerset constructions, and dual maps. Distinguishes fullness, faithfulness, and preservation versus reflection of isomorphisms, with examples showing why functors need not preserve all universal constructions.

prerequisites.reason: Uses the axioms for categories, arrows, identities and composition.

background: Elementary examples of sets, groups and functions; no advanced algebra is required.
readiness_checks: Can you state what a functor must do to identities and composites?
Can you name a structure-preserving translation that forgets some properties?
